## The falsifying observation

A later poll tick on the SAME phase, same pod, same run:

    gpu_util = 52,0,70,0

GPUs 0 and 2 at 52 percent and 70 percent. So the phase allocates CUDA contexts and does real GPU
work. The task body's central claim — that P5 ran a 4xH100 pod with no CUDA context at all — is
WRONG.

## What I actually measured, and where the inference broke

The measurement was real: 8 nvidia-smi samples over 56 s, all four GPUs at 0 percent AND 0 MiB.
The error was treating that as a property of the PHASE rather than of the 56 seconds.

P5 fans out 71 registry jobs across 4 work-conserving workers over a ~2h phase. The jobs are
heterogeneous. My window landed in a CPU-only stretch. Nothing about 0 MiB at time T constrains
time T plus 40 minutes.

The epistemic asymmetry I got backwards, stated so the next reader does not repeat it: a ZERO
utilization reading is WEAK evidence, because it only reports absence during the sampled window. A
NONZERO reading is STRONG evidence, because 52 percent and 70 percent cannot be a sampling
artifact. I leaned on a window of zeros as though it were strong, and I even reported it as
conclusive on the grounds that 0 MiB rules out sampling between kernels. That reasoning is valid
only within the window.
